threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it a latte, not a flat white, and you're clutching that takeaway cup like it's gold. Everyone else is already on to terrace glasses.
Last night on the 59, a guy serenaded the bus with old soul tunes. Half the passengers joined in, turning the ride into a makeshift karaoke session.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I found a bright orange vinyl in a secondhand shop while dodging U-Bahn delays – it felt like a hidden treasure just for us Neuköllners.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do buses and trams pause for spontaneous street festivals. You'll see the whole flex schedule shuffle when a party breaks out!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from here when they can name the exact street where the burrito truck is parked without checking their phone.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a street performer on Muni who turned a whole commute into a sing-along. Even the bus driver joined in. Only in SF!

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think 'pintxos' are everywhere here. In Gràcia, it's all about 'tapas' from the corner bodega; the real vibe is local, not trendy.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You’ll often find them using Google Maps to navigate the simplest routes around Gràcia, missing all the shortcuts locals know.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look bewildered when the 243 bus goes off-route. Regulars just shrug and hop on the nightbuses instead.
Last night on the 47, an old bloke offered the driver a pint of Best as a tip. Didn't even blink when he got turned down. Classic Bermondsey.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a kid selling homemade lemonade at Hermannplatz while the next man juggled flaming torches. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find a bustling flea market specializing in vintage DDR items and a guy selling homemade vegan döner side by side.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a real local by their grocery cart – they know to hit up the veggie stands before 6 PM for the best deals on slightly bruised avocados.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a tux playing a sax on the 6. Only in San Francisco would wedding prep include serenading strangers on Muni.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always think the squares here are for lounging. But locals hold their breath until they clear out for the evening. It’s our stage, not theirs.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they’re new when they’re still trying to figure out the difference between ‘café con leche’ and ‘café solo’ at the corner bar.
